cards.text: It's the Feast of Tabernacles in Jerusalem, and Jesus has been teaching in the temple courts (John 7:2, 14). The chief priests and Pharisees have already sent officers to arrest Him (John 7:32). Now it's the last and greatest day of the feast, and friend, the air is TENSE.
Jesus stands up and calls out in a loud voice, “If anyone is thirsty, let him come to Me and drink.” A LOUD voice, friend. Mags would be proud.

cards.question: Jesus says streams of living water will flow from within someone. Who?
John explains it for us. When Jesus talks about living water, He's speaking about the ___.
John says the Spirit hadn't been given yet when Jesus said this. Why not?

answers.text: Jesus had not yet been glorified
The feast had not ended yet
The crowd had not repented yet

cards.text: Some people hear those words and say, “This is truly the Prophet.” And just like that, the crowd turns into a group chat where EVERYBODY has a take.

cards.question: Some in the crowd call Jesus the Prophet. Others go even further. Who do they say He is?

cards.text: But still others push back, and their problem is where Jesus is from. That's like turning down the best cookie in the box because you don't like the bakery on the label.

cards.question: The doubters in the crowd ask how the Christ could come from one place. Which place?
The doubters point to Scripture. They say the Christ will come from the line of ___ and from the village of ___.

cards.text: Friend, I'm hopping up and down on my gold base over here, because Matthew 2:1 says Jesus was born in Bethlehem in Judea. The answer is RIGHT THERE.

cards.question: With all these different takes, the crowd ends up divided because of Jesus.
Some in the crowd want to seize Jesus, and someone finally lays a hand on Him.

cards.text: Now the officers head back to the chief priests and Pharisees with nothing in their hands, like showing up to the meeting without the ONE thing you were sent to get. The bosses ask, “Why didn’t you bring Him in?”

cards.question: The chief priests and Pharisees want to know why the officers didn't bring Jesus in. What do the officers say?

answers.text: Never has anyone spoken like this man
The crowd was too big to push through
He slipped away from us in the courts

cards.question: When the officers say no one has ever spoken like Jesus, the Pharisees agree and decide to go hear Him for themselves.
The Pharisees ask the officers if they've been deceived too, and whether any rulers or Pharisees have believed in Jesus. Then they say the crowd that doesn't know the law is under a ___.

cards.text: They JUST asked if any Pharisees have believed in Jesus. And then Nicodemus speaks up, a man who had gone to Jesus earlier (John 3:1-2) and who is one of them. Friend... awkward.

cards.question: Nicodemus asks the group a question about their own law. What does he ask?

answers.text: Whether it convicts a man before hearing him
Whether it lets officers arrest at a feast
Whether it allows healing on the Sabbath

cards.question: Nicodemus wants Jesus to get a fair hearing. How do the others answer him?

answers.text: They ask if he is from Galilee too
They agree to give Jesus a hearing
They send Nicodemus to question Jesus

cards.text: Then they tell him, “Look into it, and you will see that no prophet comes out of Galilee.” Hang on to your apron, friend, because this story's still got another batch in the oven.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: the quote, "A LOUD voice, friend." and "Mags would be proud." A story card other than the opening card can have only 1 or 2.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The question says "John explains it for us," which names John as the writer of the Gospel. No verse in the Gospel names its writer as John, and the card gives no reference for the claim.
findings.question: Can Papa Dorin call the Gospel's narrator "John" with no verse naming him, or should he say something like "the Gospel tells us"?

findings.problem: No card tells the baker that John 7:39 says the Spirit was one that those who believed in Jesus were later to receive. Cards 4 and 5 skip that part of the verse, but it explains who the living water is for.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: "Others go even further" ranks the claim that Jesus is the Christ above the claim that He is the Prophet. John 7:40-41 only lists the two claims side by side. The wording also hints that the answer is the biggest title on offer.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: This story card tells nothing from John 7:37-52. It is an aside about Matthew 2:1, and it does not move the baker forward through the passage.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: Card 6 already said the crowd "turns into a group chat where EVERYBODY has a take." This question then opens with "With all these different takes." Together they give away the answer that the crowd is divided (John 7:43), so the baker isn't reasoning anything out.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The right answer, "Never has anyone spoken like this man," is a statement of awe that sounds like Scripture. Both wrong answers are plain, practical excuses. The right answer stands out by its tone.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The card sets up Nicodemus as the answer to the Pharisees' question "Have any of the rulers or Pharisees believed in Him?" and then says "Friend... awkward." That suggests Nicodemus believed in Jesus, but John 7:50 only says he had gone to Jesus earlier and was one of them.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: "They JUST asked...", "And then Nicodemus speaks up..." and "Friend... awkward." A story card other than the opening card can have only 1 or 2.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: "Nicodemus wants Jesus to get a fair hearing" states what Nicodemus wants as fact. John 7:51 only gives his question.

rule.text: Feelings: He can guess at a feeling, marked as his own ("I think," "I bet"). Never as fact.
